source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which white cells arrive FIRST at a site of tissue injury?
questions.rationale: Neutrophils are first at the injury site; monocytes phagocytose in chronic injury; lymphocytes mediate immunity.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Inflammation (PDF p. 16)
questions.quote: Neutrophils — are first to be launched at the site of injury

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Injured tissue releases substances that attract phagocytes. This process is:
questions.rationale: Chemotaxis is the magnet-like attraction of phagocytes to the injured area.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Inflammation (PDF p. 16)
questions.quote: Chemotaxis — impaired tissues release substances which exert magnet-like force to the phagocytes

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A clean surgical incision with approximated edges heals by:
questions.rationale: First intention occurs in clean-cut wounds with approximated edges and minimal scarring.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Healing Process (PDF p. 16)
questions.quote: First Intention — occurs in clean-cut wound.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An infected wound is left open, then closed surgically days later. This is healing by:
questions.rationale: Third intention is delayed surgical closure of an infected wound.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Healing Process (PDF p. 16)
questions.quote: Third Intention — occurs when there is delayed surgical closure of infected wound

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An electric fan cools a febrile child. Which heat-loss process is this?
questions.rationale: Convection is dispersion of heat by air currents. Conduction needs contact; radiation needs no contact.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Heat Loss (PDF p. 17)
questions.quote: Convection - dispersion of heat by air currents

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When is body temperature normally LOWEST?
questions.rationale: Diurnal variation: lowest 4–6 am, highest 4–6 pm.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Body Temperature (PDF p. 17)
questions.quote: Lowest temp: 4am — 6am

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A fever stays above normal but swings more than 2°C within 24 hours. Which type?
questions.rationale: Remittent fever has wide fluctuations over 2°C, all above normal.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Fever (PDF p. 17)
questions.quote: Remittent fever - wide range of temp fluctuations more than 2°C for over 24 hrs, all of which are above normal

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client just drank hot coffee. How long should the nurse wait before taking an oral temperature?
questions.rationale: Wait 30 minutes after hot or cold drinks, food, or smoking.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Assessing Temperature (PDF p. 17)
questions.quote: Wait for 30 mins. before taking oral temperature

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: For which client is an ORAL temperature contraindicated?
questions.rationale: Oral temps are avoided with oral lesions, dyspnea, cough, vomiting, NGT or ET tubes, seizures, young children, and confusion.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Assessing Temperature (PDF p. 17)
questions.quote: Presence of oro-nasal pack, NGT, ET

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Rectal temperature is contraindicated in which client?
questions.rationale: Rectal temps are avoided with rectal conditions, diarrhea, quadriplegia, and MI (vagal stimulation).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Assessing Temperature (PDF p. 18)
questions.quote: Quadriplegia and Myocardial Infarction

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How is the pinna pulled for a tympanic temperature in a 2-year-old?
questions.rationale: For children under 3, the pinna is pulled straight back and slightly down; for adults, up and back.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Tympanic Temperature (PDF p. 18)
questions.quote: pull pinna straight back and slightly downward for children <3 y/o

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which is correct when giving a tepid sponge bath?
questions.rationale: TSB is done by patting to avoid friction; alcohol dries and irritates the skin.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Tepid Sponge Bath (PDF p. 18)
questions.quote: Done by patting

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client's temperature is 102.2°F. What is it in Celsius?
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Temperature Conversion (PDF p. 18)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which pulse site is used during cardiac arrest in an INFANT?
questions.rationale: The brachial pulse is used during infant cardiac arrest and for BP; carotid is used in adults.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pulse Sites (PDF p. 19)
questions.quote: Brachial- used to measure BP and used during cardiac arrest in infants

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which pulse site is routinely used for infants and children up to 3 years?
questions.rationale: The apical pulse is routine for infants and children up to 3 years.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pulse Sites (PDF p. 19)
questions.quote: Apical- routinely used for infants and children up to 3 y/o

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The apical rate is 96 and the radial rate is 84 at the same time. What is this called?
questions.rationale: Pulse deficit is the difference between apical and radial rates (here 12).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pulse Deficit (PDF p. 19)
questions.quote: Discrepancy between the apical and radial pulse

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A pulse obliterated easily with light pressure is documented as:
questions.rationale: Scale: 0 absent, 1+ weak/thready, 2+ normal, 3+ bounding.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pulse Scale (PDF p. 19)
questions.quote: 1+ - Weak or thread

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the primary chemical stimulus for breathing in healthy people?
questions.rationale: The medulla is the primary respiratory center, and CO2 is the main chemical stimulus.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Respiratory Center (PDF p. 19)
questions.quote: CO2 is the primary chemical stimuli for breathing

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Breathing that waxes from very deep to very shallow, then stops briefly, is:
questions.rationale: Cheyne-Stokes goes from very deep to very shallow followed by temporary apnea.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Respiratory Terms (PDF p. 20)
questions.quote: Cheyne-Stokes- very deep to very shallow breathing followed by temporary apnea

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client in DKA has rapid, deep, labored breathing. What is it called?
questions.rationale: Kussmaul's respirations are rapid, deep, and labored, seen in metabolic acidosis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Respiratory Terms (PDF p. 20)
questions.quote: Kussmaul's- rapid, deep and labored breathing

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A shrill, harsh sound on INSPIRATION is:
questions.rationale: Stridor is a shrill, harsh inspiratory sound; wheeze is a high-pitched expiratory sound; stertor is snoring.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Respiratory Terms (PDF p. 20)
questions.quote: Stridor- shrill, harsh sound heard during inspiration

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which error gives a FALSELY HIGH blood pressure?
questions.rationale: A narrow or loose cuff, arm below heart level, unsupported arm, or insufficient rest give false highs.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Errors in BP (PDF p. 21)
questions.quote: Bladder cuff too narrow

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How fast should the BP cuff be deflated?
questions.rationale: Release the valve at 2–3 mm Hg per second to identify Korotkoff phases.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Assessing BP (PDF p. 21)
questions.quote: Release the valve of the cuff at the rate of 2-3mmHG per second

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Pain lasting 6 months or longer is classified as:
questions.rationale: Acute pain lasts seconds to 6 months; chronic pain lasts 6 months or longer.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Pain (PDF p. 21)
questions.quote: Chronic Pain – constant or intermittent pain that lasts for 6 months or longer.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In PQRST pain assessment, 'R' refers to:
questions.rationale: PQRST: provoking factors, quality, radiation, severity, time.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Characteristics of Pain (PDF p. 21)
questions.quote: Radiation

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which pain scale suits a young child?
questions.rationale: The Faces Pain Scale is suitable for children to describe pain.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Assessment of Pain (PDF p. 22)
questions.quote: Suitable for children to describe pain

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Percussing over an emphysematous lung produces which sound?
questions.rationale: Hyperresonance (very loud, booming) is heard over emphysematous lungs; resonance over normal lung.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Percussion Sounds (PDF p. 22)
questions.quote: Hyper resonance Very loud Booming Emphysematous lung

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the correct sequence for examining the abdomen?
questions.rationale: Abdominal sequence: inspection, auscultation, percussion, palpation, so palpation does not alter bowel sounds.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Physical Exam (PDF p. 23)
questions.quote: The sequence for examination of the abdomen is as follows: (IAPePa)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When should a painful abdominal quadrant be palpated?
questions.rationale: The painful quadrant is palpated last; no palpation is done with liver or kidney tumors.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Physical Exam (PDF p. 23)
questions.quote: Palpate the painful quadrant of the abdomen last

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which breath sound is soft, low-pitched, and heard over most of the lung fields?
questions.rationale: Vesicular sounds are soft, low-pitched 'gentle sighing' sounds over the bronchioles and alveoli.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Breath Sounds (PDF p. 22)
questions.quote: Vesicular Soft-intensity,low-pitched,"gentle sighing" sounds
